Class AlgoHierarchyWriteGuard

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.service.AlgoHierarchyWriteGuard
@Service public class AlgoHierarchyWriteGuard extends Object
Keeps the strategy hierarchy read only while a request operates in a simulation environment, and keeps a single strategy read only while one of its environments is being replayed.

The hierarchy belongs to the home tenant and a replay reads it from there, which is why AlgoBaseResource re-points every algo write at getActualIdTenant(). Without this guard an edit made inside an environment would therefore silently land in the home tenant, while the limit counters counted the environment - the MAX_ALGO_* caps would be bypassable. Changes are made in the user's own portfolio and the simulation is replayed afterwards.

The guard sits in the repository implementations rather than in the resources, so that the bulk creation endpoints and every internal caller pass through it as well.

    • isSimulationContext

      public boolean isSimulationContext()
      Reports whether the current request operates in a verified simulation environment of the user's own home tenant.

      The token is not trusted on its own: the tenant row is loaded and has to be of kind TenantKindType.SIMULATION_COPY with the user's persisted home tenant as its parent. Any other mismatch between token and database is not this guard's business - the tenant context filter has already rejected such a request - so it answers false rather than producing a second, misleading refusal.

      Returns:
      true when the current tenant is a simulation environment below the user's home tenant

    • assertHierarchyWritable

      public void assertHierarchyWritable(Integer idNode)
      Refuses a mutation of the strategy hierarchy issued from a simulation environment, and a mutation of a strategy that one of the user's environments is replaying right now.

      A replay freezes the weightings when it starts but reads the strategies and their activation afresh on every trading day. An edit during the run would therefore apply to the remaining days only, and the run would no longer match the snapshot it records. Changes are made before or after the run, and the environment is replayed again.

      Parameters:
      idNode - any node of the hierarchy - top, asset class or security - or null for a node not yet created
      Throws:
      DataViolationException - if the request operates in a simulation environment, or the strategy the node belongs to is being replayed

    • assertCreateWithinLimit

      public void assertCreateWithinLimit(LimitKey limitKey, int additional)
      Refuses the creation of hierarchy nodes or strategies beyond the tenant's lifetime cap.

      The hierarchy entities are tenant private, so the generic create path checks neither a daily budget nor - because their keys are registered with checkedOnGenericCreate = false - their cap. Every repository implementation therefore calls this for a new row, which bounds the plain REST create as well as every internal caller. It must run after assertHierarchyWritable(Integer): the counter counts the tenant the request operates in, which is the home tenant only once the simulation context has been refused.

      Parameters:
      limitKey - the MAX key of the entity about to be created
      additional - how many rows of that entity the write creates
      Throws:
      DataViolationException - if the rows would exceed the configured cap
